questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding electronegativity values on the Pauling scale:
(i) Fluorine has the highest electronegativity ($4.0$), followed by Oxygen ($3.5$).
(ii) Nitrogen and Chlorine have practically identical electronegativities ($\approx 3.0$).
(iii) Carbon, Sulfur, and Iodine share approximately the same electronegativity value ($\approx 2.5$).
(iv) Phosphorus and Hydrogen have virtually identical electronegativities ($\approx 2.1$).
Which of the above statements are correct according to NCERT?
options: A) (i) and (ii) only
B) (i), (ii), and (iii) only
C) (ii) and (iv) only
D) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Review Pauling electronegativity values from NCERT:
- $\text{F} = 4.0$, $\text{O} = 3.5$. Statement (i) is correct.
- $\text{N} = 3.04 \approx 3.0$ and $\text{Cl} = 3.16 \approx 3.0$. Statement (ii) is correct.
- $\text{C} = 2.55 \approx 2.5$, $\text{S} = 2.58 \approx 2.5$, $\text{I} = 2.66 \approx 2.5$. Statement (iii) is correct.
- $\text{P} = 2.19 \approx 2.1$ and $\text{H} = 2.20 \approx 2.1$. Statement (iv) is correct.
Step 2: All four comparative statements are standard NCERT benchmark values.
Conclusion: Statements (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) are all correct.

questions.questionText:
Match the oxides of third-period elements in List I with their precise acid-base character in List II according to NCERT:
List I (Oxide)
A. $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$
B. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$
C. $\text{SiO}_2$
D. $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_7$

List II (Acid-Base Character)
I. Amphoteric
II. Strongly basic
III. Strongly acidic
IV. Weakly acidic

Choose the correct match from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
B) A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
C) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
D) A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Trace the variation of acid-base behavior of normal oxides across Period 3:
- $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$: reacts with water to form strong alkali $\text{NaOH}$; strongly basic (A-II).
- $\text{MgO}$: basic.
- $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$: reacts with both aqueous acids (forming $\text{Al}^{3+}$ salts) and strong bases (forming aluminates); amphoteric (B-I).
- $\text{SiO}_2$: giant covalent network that reacts only with hot concentrated bases; weakly acidic (C-IV).
- $\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}$: acidic.
- $\text{SO}_3$: strongly acidic.
- $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_7$: dissolves in water to form perchloric acid $\text{HClO}_4$; very strongly acidic (D-III).
Step 2: Combine matches: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.
Conclusion: The correct match is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements regarding neutral and amphoteric oxides:
Statement I: Carbon monoxide ($\text{CO}$), nitric oxide ($\text{NO}$), and nitrous oxide ($\text{N}_2\text{O}$) are neutral oxides that exhibit neither acidic nor basic properties.
Statement II: Beryllium oxide ($\text{BeO}$), zinc oxide ($\text{ZnO}$), aluminium oxide ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$), and lead(II) oxide ($\text{PbO}$) are amphoteric oxides that dissolve in both acids and alkalis.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:
options: A) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
D) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Oxides that do not react with either acids or bases to form salts are called neutral oxides. In NCERT, the non-metal oxides $\text{CO}, \text{NO}$, and $\text{N}_2\text{O}$ are explicitly classified as neutral oxides. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Oxides that react with both acids (behaving as basic oxides) and bases (behaving as acidic oxides) are termed amphoteric oxides. Elements located near the boundary between metals and non-metals or with high charge-to-radius ratios form amphoteric oxides. Key NCERT examples include $\text{BeO}, \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3, \text{Ga}_2\text{O}_3, \text{ZnO}, \text{PbO}, \text{PbO}_2, \text{SnO}$, and $\text{SnO}_2$. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): While phosphorus forms pentachloride ($\text{PCl}_5$) and aluminium forms hexafluoroaluminate ($[\text{AlF}_6]^{3-}$), nitrogen cannot form pentahalides ($\text{NCl}_5$) and boron cannot form $[\text{BF}_6]^{3-}$.
Reason (R): Second-period elements have only four valence orbitals ($2s, 2p_x, 2p_y, 2p_z$) and lack vacant $d$-orbitals, restricting their maximum covalency to 4, whereas third-period elements have accessible vacant $3d$ orbitals allowing expansion of their valence shells.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) (A) is true but (R) is false.
B) (A) is false but (R) is true.
C) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
D) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Second-period elements like Nitrogen ($Z = 7$) and Boron ($Z = 5$) have an octet limit and maximum coordination number / covalency of 4 ($[\text{BF}_4]^-$ is formed, but $[\text{BF}_6]^{3-}$ is impossible; $\text{NF}_3$ is formed, but $\text{NF}_5$ or $\text{NCl}_5$ cannot exist). In contrast, third-period counterparts Phosphorus and Aluminium have available $3d$ orbitals, allowing expansion beyond an octet to form $\text{PCl}_5$ and $[\text{AlF}_6]^{3-}$. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). In the $n = 2$ shell, only $l = 0$ ($2s$) and $l = 1$ ($2p$) orbitals exist, giving a total of $1 + 3 = 4$ orbitals capable of accommodating at most 8 electrons in covalent bonds. There are no $2d$ orbitals. For $n = 3$, $3d$ orbitals are energetically available for hybridization ($sp^3d, sp^3d^2$), enabling covalencies of 5 and 6. Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding multiple bonding in second-period elements:
Statement I: The first member of each group in the p-block (e.g., $\text{C}, \text{N}, \text{O}$) displays a remarkable ability to form $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds with itself and with other small, highly electronegative atoms.
Statement II: Heavier congeners of the same groups (e.g., $\text{Si}, \text{P}, \text{S}$) form strong and stable $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds because their larger $3p$ orbitals allow more extensive lateral overlap.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:
options: A) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
D) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. The second-period p-block elements ($\text{C}, \text{N}, \text{O}$) have very small atomic sizes, which allows their $2p$ orbitals to approach close enough for effective lateral (sideways) overlap, forming stable $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds (e.g., $\text{C}=\text{C}, \text{C}\equiv\text{C}, \text{C}=\text{O}, \text{N}\equiv\text{N}$). Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. For heavier congeners like $\text{Si}, \text{P}$, and $\text{S}$, the atomic orbitals ($3p$) are much larger and more diffuse. The larger internuclear distance prevents effective sideways overlap; consequently, $p\pi-p\pi$ multiple bonds are very weak and unstable. Instead, these heavier elements prefer single bonds, forming catenated networks or cyclic molecules (e.g., $\text{SiO}_2$ giant covalent polymer vs $\text{CO}_2$ gas; $\text{P}_4$ tetrahedral solid vs $\text{N}_2$ diatomic triple-bonded gas). Thus, Statement II is incorrect.
Conclusion: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Lithium exhibits properties that are strikingly similar to magnesium, and beryllium shows remarkable chemical similarities to aluminium (diagonal relationship).
Reason (R): Moving diagonally across the periodic table, the increase in size going down a group is approximately compensated by the decrease in size going from left to right across a period, resulting in nearly identical polarizing power ($\text{charge}/\text{radius}$ ratio).
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
B) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
C) (A) is true but (R) is false.
D) (A) is false but (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). The first element of Group 1 ($\text{Li}$) resembles the second element of Group 2 ($\text{Mg}$), and the first element of Group 2 ($\text{Be}$) resembles the second element of Group 13 ($\text{Al}$). This diagonal resemblance is well-documented in NCERT as the diagonal relationship. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Moving across a period (left to right), ionic size decreases and charge increases, so polarizing power (ionic potential $\phi = \frac{q}{r}$) increases. Moving down a group (top to bottom), ionic size increases and polarizing power decreases. When moving diagonally (one step down and one step to the right), these two opposing factors cancel each other out. As a result, diagonally related pairs have nearly identical charge-to-radius ratios, polarizing powers, and electronegativities, leading to similar chemical behavior. Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.questionText:
Which of the following chemical similarities between Beryllium ($\text{Be}$) and Aluminium ($\text{Al}$) arise as a direct consequence of their diagonal relationship?
(i) Both $\text{Be}$ and $\text{Al}$ form oxides ($\text{BeO}$ and $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) and hydroxides that are amphoteric in nature.
(ii) Both metals are rendered passive by concentrated nitric acid due to the formation of an imperviously protective oxide surface film.
(iii) The anhydrous chlorides $\text{BeCl}_2$ and $\text{AlCl}_3$ have chloro-bridged polymeric/dimeric structures in the vapor/solid phase and act as strong Lewis acids.
(iv) Both $\text{Be}^{2+}$ and $\text{Al}^{3+}$ have a strong tendency to form fluoro-complexes such as $[\text{BeF}_4]^{2-}$ and $[\text{AlF}_6]^{3-}$.
Choose the correct option from below:
options: A) (ii) and (iv) only
B) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)
C) (i), (ii), and (iii) only
D) (i) and (iii) only
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Check property (i). Unlike other Group 2 oxides which are strongly basic, $\text{BeO}$ is amphoteric, just like $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$. Both dissolve in acids and in alkali solutions (forming beryllates and aluminates). This statement is correct.
Step 2: Check property (ii). Both metals are not readily attacked by concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ due to the rapid formation of a passive, impervious oxide layer on the metal surface. This statement is correct.
Step 3: Check property (iii). Both $\text{BeCl}_2$ and $\text{AlCl}_3$ exhibit covalent character, exist as bridged species ($\text{BeCl}_2$ as chloro-bridged chains in solid and dimers in vapor phase; $\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6$ as dimer), and function as potent Lewis acids used in Friedel-Crafts alkylation/acylation reactions. This statement is correct.
Step 4: Check property (iv). Both cations have high charge-to-radius ratios and coordinate readily with fluoride ions to form stable fluoro-complex anions: $[\text{BeF}_4]^{2-}$ and $[\text{AlF}_6]^{3-}$. This statement is correct.
Conclusion: All four statements (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv) are correct.

questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding periodicity in chemical reactivity across the periodic table:
Statement I: Maximum chemical reactivity in the periodic table is displayed at the two extremes—by the alkali metals on the extreme left (which readily lose electrons due to low ionization enthalpy) and by the halogens on the extreme right (which readily gain electrons due to strongly negative electron gain enthalpy).
Statement II: The oxides of elements on the extreme left of the periodic table are strongly basic (e.g., $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$), whereas the oxides of elements on the extreme right (excluding noble gases) are strongly acidic (e.g., $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_7$).
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer:
options: A) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
B) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In any period of the periodic table, chemical reactivity is greatest at the two extremities. Elements on the far left (Group 1 alkali metals) have the lowest ionization enthalpies and exhibit extreme reactivity by losing electrons to form cations. Elements on the far right (Group 17 halogens) have the most negative electron gain enthalpies and highest electronegativities, reacting vigorously by gaining electrons to form anions. Elements in the center of the table show intermediate reactivity. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Metallic character is highest on the extreme left; metallic oxides are basic anhydrides (e.g., $\text{Na}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to 2\text{NaOH}$). Non-metallic character is highest on the extreme right; non-metallic oxides are acidic anhydrides (e.g., $\text{Cl}_2\text{O}_7 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \to 2\text{HClO}_4$). Oxides transition from strongly basic on the left, to amphoteric/neutral in the middle, to strongly acidic on the right. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
